clue.text: Medic bandages male American sea creature

indicators.note: to bandage something is to wrap round it, so the first word encloses the next

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A doctor dressing the wounds of an American man who has met some creature of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bandages' reads as a noun but is a verb here: the doctor wraps round the male, and the American is added on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A grampus is a cetacean, usually Risso's dolphin or loosely the killer whale, so a marine animal.

clue.text: German consumed half of relative's cake

indicators.note: taking only half of the word means the second half is cut away

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A German guest scoffs half of an aunt's cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A gâteau is a rich layered cream cake, from the French word for cake.

clue.text: Surgically remove a belt twisted round bottom of tibia

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, enclosing it
twisted letters are bent out of their original order
in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: An operation to take away a strap wrapped around the lower leg bone.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine to ablate is to cut away or destroy tissue, i.e. excise it in surgery.

clue.text: Minor fairy meeting pantheon's foremost goddess by lake

indicators.note: pieces meeting are placed side by side in sequence

parts.note: a peri is a fairy of Persian myth

indicators.note: the foremost letter is the one at the front of the word

parts.note: Hera is the Greek queen of the gods
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A lesser sprite encounters the leading goddess of the gods beside some water.
explanation.definitionFit: Peripheral issues are on the edge rather than central, so of little importance.

clue.text: Turf small part of hospital site

parts.note: a ward is a section of a hospital

explanation.surface: Grass laid on a little corner of the hospital grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turf' reads as a verb, to throw out, but it is the noun for grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Sward is an expanse of short grass, the same as a lawn of turf.

clue.text: Old lady tiring of dog

parts.note: one's old lady is one's mother, ma
a stiff climb or task is hard going and tiring

explanation.surface: An elderly woman worn out by walking her dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The mastiff is a large, powerful breed of guard dog.

clue.text: Spoil good American girl with cocktail

explanation.surface: Ruining a nice American girl's evening with a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A margarita is a tequila-based drink served with lime and a salted rim, a mixed drink.

clue.text: Retired thief asked to steal money box

indicators.note: something retired withdraws, going back the way it came
the letters are stolen, lifted out of the run of text

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A former burglar was asked to rob a strongbox.
explanation.definitionFit: A safe is a secure locked box for keeping money and valuables.

clue.text: Setter going to university before new art eclipses old impressionist

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as I

indicators.note: to eclipse is to cover something over, hiding it within
a new version of the word means its letters are made over

explanation.surface: A puzzle-setter goes to college before fresh art outshines an old Impressionist painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressionist' suggests Monet, but here it is a mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: An impressionist is an entertainer who mimics famous people, i.e. one who copies others.

clue.text: Trap set by crafty secretary upset salesman

parts.note: fly is slang for sharp or cunning

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down, reading it from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A snare laid by a cunning secretary has upset a travelling salesman.
explanation.definitionFit: Flypaper is sticky paper hung up to catch insects, so it is a type of snare.

clue.text: Tradesman's bill finally set in order

indicators.note: something set in another is placed inside it

parts.note: a tier is a rank or level in an order

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A workman's invoice finally gets put right.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition and wordplay; L goes inside TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiler is a building tradesman who lays tiles on roofs, floors and walls.

clue.text: Insubstantial fabulous creature heading off with another

indicators.note: with its heading off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a fairy is a creature of fable
another of the same creature, this time whole

explanation.surface: A flimsy fairy-tale being losing its head alongside a second one.
explanation.definitionFit: Airy-fairy describes ideas that are vague, impractical and lacking solid substance.

clue.text: Australian disputed point with college fellow from New Zealand

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for Australian

indicators.note: a disputed word is argued over and pulled about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a dean is a senior fellow of a college

explanation.surface: An Australian arguing a point with an academic who hails from New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Australian' looks like the definition, and the answer would fit it, but it supplies only the single letter A; the definition is at the other end.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipodean means belonging to the Antipodes, Australia and New Zealand, as seen from Britain.

clue.text: Scrap a musical genre

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: Getting rid of a whole style of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A raga is a melodic framework in Indian classical music, so a style or form of music.

clue.text: Cook holding Defoe's novel is annoyed and disappointed

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside it
novel means new, so the letters take a new form

parts.note: fodder for the rearrangement, including the S

explanation.surface: A cook reading Robinson Crusoe is fed up with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a nod to Defoe's books but signals the rearrangement; Daniel Defoe wrote Robinson Crusoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheesed off is British slang for irritated and fed up.

clue.text: Hero singles out traditional beauty

indicators.note: letters out of place are scattered and must be put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A champion picks out an old-fashioned looker.
explanation.definitionFit: An English rose is a fair-skinned, classically pretty English woman, the stock image of conventional good looks.

clue.text: Landlady hiding first part of takings in dress in rundown area

indicators.note: one piece hides the other inside it

parts.note: a landlady is a host to her lodgers

indicators.note: the first part of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A landlady stashing some of the till money in her frock in a seedy neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: HOST hides T (HOST-T), and the result sits inside the dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost town is a deserted, decaying settlement, an extreme case of a run-down place.

clue.text: Stopped to question editor after expense account's reverse engineered

indicators.note: engineered in reverse means the two items are put together in the opposite order to the clue

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: An editor collared over an expenses claim that was cooked backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expense account' is swapped round to account + expense, and editor comes after.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to approach and stop them, typically to speak to them boldly.

clue.text: Turn away from boxer with neat manoeuvre close to rope

indicators.note: a manoeuvre moves things around, so these letters change places
the close of a word is its end, so the final letter is used

explanation.surface: A boxer slips away from the ropes with a deft move.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate people is to estrange them, making them hostile or causing them to withdraw.

clue.text: Work in association with colonel, having left sailor to speak

parts.note: an AB is an able seaman
to orate is to make a speech

explanation.surface: A colonel who has abandoned a seaman wants a word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work in association with' reads as the full definition, but 'with' is the joining word and the wordplay starts at 'colonel'.
explanation.definitionFit: To collaborate is to labour jointly with others on a shared project.

clue.text: Chaps receiving help recovered from unproductive bowling spell

indicators.note: the chaps receive the help, taking it in between them

parts.note: once you have recovered from an illness you are over it

explanation.surface: Men getting assistance after a poor stretch of play.
explanation.walkthrough: M(AID)EN + OVER. In cricket an over is six balls bowled in a row; a maiden over is one from which the batsman scores no runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden over yields no runs, so it is a spell of bowling that produces nothing for the batting side.

clue.text: Boisterous girls on a night out ignoring new prince

indicators.note: letters ignored are left out of the word

parts.note: a hen party is a celebration for a bride-to-be and her women friends

explanation.surface: A rowdy bunch of women out on the town shunning a young royal.
explanation.walkthrough: A hen party (or hen night) is the British name for a bachelorette party.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty means loud, vigorous and full of energy, close to rumbustious.

clue.text: See 19
No-win situation involving black neighbour of Black Beauty?

indicators.note: the situation involves the colour, drawing it inside itself

parts.note: in chess, stalemate is a draw where nobody wins
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A deadlock involving a dark-coated horse next door to the famous fictional one.
explanation.walkthrough: Black Beauty is the horse in Anna Sewell's novel; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A stablemate is a horse housed in the same stable, so a neighbour of any particular horse.

clue.text: Snub Indian bearing facial decoration

indicators.note: the words bear the answer, carrying it within them

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Ignoring someone from India by the look on their face.
explanation.definitionFit: A bindi is a decorative dot worn on the forehead, especially by Hindu women.

clue.text: Slide for special child

explanation.surface: A playground slide for a child with special needs.
explanation.definitionFit: To skid is to slip or slide uncontrollably on a surface.

clue.text: Find place to store luggage close to hand in Ipswich, say

indicators.note: the earlier pieces sit inside the place named after this word

parts.note: Ipswich is a town in Suffolk, an example of the class
a luggage rack on a train

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: Searching for somewhere to put your bags near at hand in a Suffolk town.
explanation.definitionFit: To track down is to locate something after a search, i.e. to find it.

clue.text: Old king rejected communist's command

parts.note: R for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so this word runs the other way

explanation.surface: An elderly monarch turns down a Marxist's instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: An order is an instruction that must be obeyed, the same as a command.

clue.text: Almost finish study of city

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to dress stone or timber is to give it a finish
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: Nearly done with researching an urban area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish' looks like the deletion signal with 'almost', but it is the word that loses a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresden is the capital of Saxony in eastern Germany, a major urban centre.

clue.text: Popular taste for period of innocence?

parts.note: what is in is fashionable or popular
a fancy for something is a taste or liking for it

explanation.surface: A craze from a more innocent era.
explanation.definitionFit: Infancy is early childhood, the time of life before experience, hence the question mark.
